findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation only drops diagnostics whose Location is in source but belongs to another compilation. Diagnostics with Location.None (metadata/null location, e.g. from FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation() returning null) have IsInSource false and are still reported. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 (an Error per L2) for a member lacking [Key] is now emitted with no location in the user's build. Previously the type would crash; now a metadata type that lacks keys could fail the user's build with a location-less error, contradicting L8 (referenced types are deliberately not analysed).

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer/generator test: lib defines generic struct Item<T> with a public member lacking [Key]/[IgnoreMember] inside [MessagePackObject], compiled to a metadata reference; app has Cmd with Item<int> member. Assert no MsgPack004 diagnostic (or any Location.None diagnostic) is reported in app. Expect failure with the current filter since !IsInSource is true.

findings.claim: The new filter is applied to all reportDiagnostic calls in TypeCollector, not just the crashing paths. Any diagnostic previously reported with a location in a different syntax tree/compilation is now silently dropped. Existing users could lose diagnostics they used to see, such as source-declared types in another compilation or linked/multi-project cases. This is a behavior change for analyzer output without opt-in.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003/004/005/etc. tests) at head and compare against base; add a case where the diagnostic location is in a tree not in compilation.SyntaxTrees and verify whether the diagnostic was previously reported.
